text: Sami turned around super fast.
summary: ja: '超速攻で' (super fast attack/immediate) is unnatural for physical movement speed → changed to '超速攻で' to '超高速で' or '超速で' for better flow; ko: '뒤를 돌아봤어' implies looking back rather than turning the whole body → changed to '뒤를 돌았어' for 'turned around'.

text: What did this pink candy taste like?
summary: ru: grammatical gender mismatch (the verb was feminine but the noun is feminine, however the instrumental case was incorrectly formed) → fixed to 'Каким на вкус была' to 'Какой на вкус была' or more naturally 'Какова была на вкус эта розовая конфета?'; ar: grammatical gender mismatch (the adjective 'pink' was masculine while the noun 'candy' is feminine) → fixed 'الورديّ' to 'الوردية'.

text: He held his breath while watching the match.
summary: pt: 'segurou o fôlego' is a literal translation of 'held'; 'prendeu a respiração' is the natural idiomatic expression for holding one's breath in Portuguese.

text: He needs to get a grip of himself.
summary: ja: phrasing was too formal/stiff for 'informal' register → changed to a more natural idiomatic expression; zh: '振作起来' implies cheering up/recovering from failure, whereas 'get a grip' usually implies self-control or stopping emotional outbursts → adjusted to '冷静点' or '克制'.

text: Put some ice on your ankle to keep the swelling down.
summary: fr: 'faire dégonfler l'enflure' is redundant → changed to 'réduire l'enflure'; it: 'far sgonfiare il gonfiore' is redundant → changed to 'ridurre il gonfiore'; de: 'lindern' (soothe) is less accurate for physical reduction of swelling → changed to 'reduzieren'; sv: 'vrist' can mean wrist or ankle, 'fotled' is more precise for ankle → changed to 'fotled'

text: You can study no matter how old you are.
summary: fr: changed 'On' to 'Tu' to match the singular addressee metadata; de: changed 'Man' to 'Du' to match the singular addressee metadata; it: changed impersonal 'Si può' to 'Puoi' to match the singular addressee metadata; ru: added 'ты' for better flow in the first clause to match the direct 'You' address.

text: Their marriage was a happy one.
summary: fr: used passé composé which implies a completed event rather than a state → changed to imparfait 'était' for a descriptive past state; it: used passato prossimo → changed to imperfetto 'era' to better reflect the descriptive nature of the English sentence.
